claims.text: Two-stage aging of a NbMoTaW-based refractory high-entropy alloy will generate uniformly dispersed nanometer-scale coherent carbide precipitates.
The precipitates generated by aging will include carbides such as TaC or NbC.
The coherent carbide precipitates will inhibit dislocation motion.
Two-stage aging will enhance high-temperature yield strength by 25–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
Two-stage aging will enhance creep resistance by 25–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The aging treatment will preserve room-temperature ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The aging treatment will cause only a minimal density increase.
The initial alloy is a coarse-grained BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy contains no significant secondary precipitates.
Aging at approximately 800°C for several hours will initiate carbide precipitation.
Subsequent aging at approximately 600°C will refine and stabilize the carbide precipitates.
The controlled two-stage heat treatment will preserve a ductile BCC matrix at room temperature.
The precipitates will remain stable and finely dispersed under the stated high-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanical benefits will hold at approximately 800–900°C under cyclic and constant loading.
The stated temperature and loading conditions simulate jet-turbine operating environments.
Precipitate coarsening during extended high-temperature exposure could diminish the strengthening effect.
Failure to control the aging parameters may cause deviations from the expected mechanical benefits.
